claims.text: Laser cladding equimolar WNbMoTaV onto TC4 at approximately 3.5 kW will produce a dense coating.
The coating produced at approximately 3.5 kW will be metallurgically bonded to TC4.
The coating will consist primarily of a refined BCC solid solution.
Substrate dilution will produce a modest Ti-rich phase in the coating.
A laser power of approximately 3.5 kW minimizes unfused powder and coating defects.
A laser power of approximately 3.5 kW limits excessive substrate dilution and over-burning.
Lattice distortion in the BCC solid solution strengthens the coating.
Grain refinement and grain-boundary strengthening increase the coating's mechanical strength.
The BCC solid solution has high resistance to plastic deformation that contributes to increased hardness and wear resistance.
A protective tribo-oxide layer forms during sliding.
The protective tribo-oxide layer contributes to enhanced wear resistance.
Insufficient laser power leaves unfused material or defects in the coating.
Excessive laser power increases substrate dilution and impairs coating structural integrity.
The approximately 3.5 kW coating will significantly increase surface microhardness relative to bare TC4.
The approximately 3.5 kW coating will reduce wear-volume loss relative to bare TC4.
Hardness and wear performance depend nonmonotonically on laser power, with an optimum near 3.5 kW.
Bare TC4 has an average hardness of approximately 341.25 HV0.3.
Bare TC4 has a wear-volume loss of 6.09 × 10^7 μm3 under the stated wear conditions.
The coating will retain TC4's existing beneficial properties.
Laser powers such as 3.1 or 3.9 kW may fail to provide the desired hardening and wear resistance.

contradictions.description: The proposed hardness test uses a 0.98 N load, corresponding to HV0.1, whereas the quoted untreated-TC4 baseline is reported as HV0.3. The baseline field nevertheless says the substrate will be tested under identical conditions, so the quoted hardness baseline is not directly condition-matched.
